name: Wrangler Manifest
purpose: The repo-root deploy-configuration file (`wrangler.toml` or `wrangler.jsonc`) as loaded, validated, and exposed to the Deploy Adapter. Parses the manifest into an object the adapter and the CI gates consult, enforces the shape rules (required top-level keys, declared bindings, no inline secrets, no collapsed URLs), and refuses malformed or leaky manifests loudly.
responsibilities: Parse `wrangler.toml` (or `wrangler.jsonc`) at the repo root; refuse absence with `WRANGLER_MANIFEST_MISSING` (AC-12101-1).

Validate the top-level keys `name`, `main`, `compatibility_date` are present and correctly typed; validate `main` resolves to an existing entry file; validate `compatibility_date` matches `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` (AC-12101-1).

Cross-check every binding name referenced from the Worker source (via env-accessor scans keyed by binding name) against the manifest declarations; refuse a missing declaration with `WRANGLER_BINDING_UNDECLARED` naming the offending source path and the missing binding (AC-12101-2).

Refuse a manifest that carries any inline secret value; scan the parsed object for keys under the vendor's secret-declaration primitive whose value is not an empty declaration (AC-12101-3, AC-12106-1).
Refuse a manifest whose production route stanza resolves to the same host as the preview alias URL with `DEPLOY_URL_COLLAPSED` (AC-12105-2).
Expose a `bindings()` accessor listing every declared binding (kind, name) for downstream consumers.
Expose a `productionUrl()` accessor deriving the production URL from the `routes`/`route`/`workers_dev`/custom-domain declaration.
internalStructure: One parser module per format (TOML and JSONC), one validator that walks the parsed object against the shape rules, one binding-usage scanner that walks the Worker source AST for env-accessor patterns, and one URL-derivation module that inspects the routes stanza. All pure functions; no I/O outside the initial file read.

interfaces.name: manifestFile
interfaces.description: Reads `wrangler.toml` or `wrangler.jsonc` at the repo root. The file's presence is required; the file's format is autodetected from the extension.

interfaces.name: workerSourceScanner
interfaces.description: AST or regex scanner over the Worker source tree that emits every binding name referenced through env-accessor patterns (for the default JS/TS Worker, `env.<NAME>.<method>` and `process.env.<NAME>` are both matched).

interfaces.name: bindings
interfaces.description: Structured list of declared bindings emitted for downstream consumers. Each entry names the binding kind (KV, D1, R2, Durable Object, static assets, var, secret, service, queue) and the binding name.

interfaces.name: productionUrl
interfaces.description: Returns the production URL derived from the manifest. When multiple routes are declared, returns the ordered list; when `workers_dev = true`, returns the workers.dev host.

tradeoffs: The loader owns validation but does not own the vendor's own manifest-level validation (which happens later at the vendor CLI). Two-stage validation means a manifest that passes this loader can still fail the vendor's own load; the trade keeps the loader project-local and fast (no vendor round-trip on every CI step) while catching the classes this blueprint cares about (undeclared bindings, inline secrets, collapsed URLs) before the vendor call. A project can point the loader at a project-authored TOML dialect (a preprocessor step) by wrapping the manifestFile interface.
